reasons: F01, F02, F03: material weakness in internal control disclosed, with no auditor ICFR attestation, so the controls over reporting are weak and nobody outside management has tested them
F04, F21, R16: going concern doubt, plus a capital raise and securities issuance in the year, creates financing pressure and a motive to present results favourably
F05, F14: auditor change within two years and a CEO/CFO change in the year signal governance instability, a classic red-flag pair
F11: material related-party transactions raise the risk of non-arm's-length dealings and undisclosed or mis-measured transactions

F22, R13: a major acquisition in the year, with soft assets about 97% of total assets, means the balance sheet rests on judgmental items (goodwill/intangibles) that are prone to overstatement in purchase price allocation and impairment testing

R04, R02, R15: sales grew about 542x from a near-zero base, gross margin deteriorated (GMI 3.08) and ROA changed a lot. This looks like an early-stage or shell company transformed by acquisition, where revenue recognition and consolidation accounting are error-prone
R05: DEPI 2.34 means depreciation rates are falling relative to assets, which could flatter earnings
F24: critical audit matter disclosed (topic 'other'), so the auditor flagged an area of high judgment

Mitigating: F06, F07, F16, F17, F18, F19 show no disagreements with the auditor, no restatement, no SEC/government investigation, no class action and no covenant issues. R17 F-score of 0.0 is low, but many ratios (R01, R03, R08, R09, R10, R19) are n/a, which limits how much weight the quantitative screen can carry
